questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Wanted to use french in an academic setting and live in Paris.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very difficult. No information from Sorbonne until the semester had already begun. Copenhagen University was not of very much assistance. Felt very lost in the beginning. No idea how to sign up for classes, wasn't invited to any orientation for incoming exchange students. Didn't get any "Welcome to Sorbonne" mails, letters, anything. Wandered helplessly around the halls of the university the first days of the semester hoping to find information, but found none.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Had a meeting with a coordinator who gave me my student ID and briefly explained how I could choose courses.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Had no orientation and received no information before the semester had already begun. Very stressful not to know what's expected of you. Started classes a week and half too late.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Idk, found something through family connections.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Sorbonne has multiple campuses all over the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Housing in Paris is expensive. I didn't get accepted at Cité U, which is student housing, so had to find something on my own.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was awfully confusing. No information beforehand. You have to send e-mails individually to the UFR (institut) AND to the professors. Course registrations happens in september - which would have been nice to know, so I wasn't worried that something was wrong with my file since I hadn't been invited to register for courses.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Course registration starts after classes start. So you can attend classes even if you haven't registred formally. It was very confusing, had to send lots of e-mails to different people and fill out forms on paper to register.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Haha, not sure there was any.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Ended up with different courses than I had planned beforehand, but all good with the ones I picked when I was in Paris.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just know that registration happens in september. For the rest, french bureaucracy is an experience, but no way around it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Had courses in both level L1, L2 and L3 (1st year, 2nd year, 3rd year). All were interesting and challenging.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different. No reading to do before classes, but sometimes homework assignments. The professor gives a lecture and you write down what they say. No discussions, and students aren't really asked to participate. More tests during the semester - usually 2 per course.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Grammaire et histoire de la langue française
2. Linguistique diachronique
3. Linguistique française 
4. Apprentissage de la programmation
5. Sociologie des migrations

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: My favorite course was Linguistique diachronique, especially the TD with Géraldine Veysseyre, where we looked at how french has evolved from latin to old french to modern french.

Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: We weren't asked to buy any books, so no spending needed for university. Paris is expensive  - going out, doing things... Lots of museums are free if you're under 25.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Didn't feel like they were any. Wasn't made aware of any - maybe because I wasn't invited to an orientation in the beginning of the semester? Didn't make a lot of friends at the university.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't know

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take daytrips og weekend trips with the train or TGV. You can get cheap tickets and there are so many beautiful cities worth visiting in France just a few hours from Paris. I visited Rouen with a friend and loved it.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I grew up in Paris, so I wasn't all new to the city.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Perhaps ask them to show you something or explain something. People are sweet and helpful.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The rigidness of the bureaucracy is very frustrating when you're danish and used to everything being centralized and fairly easy to access and understand.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Parisians go out a lot to restaurants, bars, cafés. Meeting with friends on a "terrasse" for a drink or a coffee - lovely.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Don't stress about registration before you get to Paris. It happens after courses start - that's all normal. You can attend lectures you think you want to sign up for.
2. Make sure to pick at least one course on L3 level, because they're usually taught on the old campus which is such a beautiful old building and the lecture halls are so impressive. Usually L1 and L2 will be at the other campuses.
3. If you're going on the 4EU+ program, they might not invite you to the Erasmus orientation. Maybe ask if they can include you or something. They considered this program to be different when I was there.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Just being in Paris and going to classes at the old Sorbonne. Woah, what a life.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Figuring out all the administrative stuff was frustrating and took much longer than I thought. Didn't get my Erasmus Grant until november.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
